title: Write each audit event once, in the order it arrived

blocks.text: The audit service collects events from several collectors. A collector that times out sends its whole batch again, so one event can reach the importer two or three times, each copy stamped with the time it was received. Auditors read the log top to bottom and expect each event once, in the order the events reached us.

`AuditImport` already writes a batch to the log. Finish `firstOfEach(...)` in `src/main/java/practice/AuditImport.java`: it returns each event of the batch once, as the first copy that arrived, in the order of first arrival, and leaves the batch it was given unchanged. About three lines.
Copies of an event are the same event when their ids are equal; nothing else about them has to match.

cases.says: a batch with a repeated event writes each event once and reports how many it wrote
the batch the importer received is not changed
the events are written in the order of their first arrival, not in an order the importer's own bookkeeping gives
when an event arrives twice, the copy written is the first one, not the last
two copies of an event are the same event by id, even when their receipt times differ

origin.section: A Hash Set Iterates in Hash Order, and the Order Changes as the Set Grows

concepts: A HashSet or HashMap iterates in the order of its hash table, which is not insertion order and changes when the table resizes; LinkedHashSet and LinkedHashMap keep first-insertion order.
